DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum

Based on the central necrotic base, irregular purplish borders, and the absence of red streaks or fever despite significant tenderness, this presentation is highly suggestive of Pyoderma Gangrenosum rather than a simple bacterial infection. The presence of dilated tortuous veins and pitting edema also raises the possibility of an underlying venous stasis component.
